1	# Installed harness
     2	
     3	**The real skill files live in [`skills/`](./skills/).** Loaders are directory links to that folder:
     4	
     5	- Codex — reads `.agents/skills` natively; no link needed.
     6	- Claude Code — `.claude/skills` → `../.agents/skills`
     7	- Cursor — `.cursor/skills` → `../.agents/skills`
     8	
     9	This repository consumes its own method the way a recipient project does: the same `.agents/skills`
    10	layout as Meteoscape and Forecast Collector, with this project's facts in `<project-local>` blocks.
    11	
    12	The links are tracked as symlinks (mode 120000). Git for Windows writes `core.symlinks=false` on
    13	clone, so they check out as text files. After clone, in this repo only:
    14	
    15	```
    16	git config --local core.symlinks true
    17	git checkout -- .claude/skills .cursor/skills
    18	```
    19	
    20	Windows needs Developer Mode (Settings → System → For developers) or an elevated prompt to create
    21	a directory symlink. If checkout still yields a file, delete it and run
    22	`mklink /D .claude\skills ..\.agents\skills` (likewise for `.cursor\skills`). Creating these links
    23	is part of the installer's job once it exists; a junction is not an acceptable substitute, git
    24	would track it as a directory.
    25	
    26	Which links are actually required is untested. Codex needs none; Cursor documents reading
    27	`.agents/skills` directly; Claude Code may too. The host trials in
    28	[01-0010.0020](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0020-live-alignment-across-hosts.md) settle it.
    29	
    30	## What is installed
    31	
    32	Bootstrap slices [01-0010.0020](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0020-live-alignment-across-hosts.md),
    33	[01-0010.0030](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0030-install-ticket.md),
    34	[01-0010.0035](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0035-install-spec.md),
    35	[01-0010.0040](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0040-install-plan.md),
    36	[01-0010.0050](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0050-install-implement.md),
    37	[01-0010.0060](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0060-install-verify.md), and
    38	[01-0010.0070](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0070-install-maintain.md): `align` (with its ADR, ARCH, EDGE
    39	and GLOSSARY format shelf), `impact`, `ticket` (with `TICKET-FORMAT.md`), `spec`, `plan`,
    40	`implement`, `tdd` (with its five files), `improve-comments`, `verify`, and `maintain`, from
    41	Meteoscape with the Forecast Collector `/plan` body, per the
    42	[source selection](../docs/tickets/01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#bootstrap-corpus-selection).
    43	`maintain` composes the selected `denoise` and `sync-arch` and adds the `<temporary>` enumerator.
    44	
    45	[01-0010.0090](../docs/tickets/done/01-0010.0090-install-discover.md) adds `discover` (with its
    46	`EVIDENCE.md`). It came from a different estate and so is not in the audited source selection above,
    47	which records only what was taken from Meteoscape, Forecast Collector and DriftSense; that ticket is
    48	its authority. It is used the way `impact` is — run it, use what comes back in the work at hand —
    49	and files nothing.
    50	
    51	[01-0010.0100](../docs/tickets/01-0010.0100-remaining-named-corpus.md) adds `advise`,
    52	`celebrate`, `commit` and `skill-up`, brought in by the user on 2026-09-07 ahead of that
    53	ticket's align because they are useful as they stand. They are installed and listed here; what
    54	the ticket still owes for them is on the ticket, and `/edge` — its fifth — has not arrived.
    55	`commit`'s `<project-local>` block arrived carrying another project's gate set; it was deleted
    56	rather than rewritten, because only global practice belongs in a core skill.
    57	
    58	`dream` arrived the same day. It is not one of `01-0010.0100`'s five — it comes from the parent's
    59	own backlog, beside `/recall`, `/conclude`, `/review-architecture` and `/setup-devops`, of which
    60	the other four have not arrived. [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) already describes it: optional, runs
    61	after `/conclude`, writes dreams that `/maintain` and `/align` may pick up, never amends rules.
    62	
    63	The pre-audit July corpus is kept under [`legacy/skills`](../legacy/skills/) as evidence only. Nothing loads it.
    64	
    65	## Mechanical support
    66	
    67	[`scripts/`](./scripts/) holds what `/maintain` derives and repairs mechanically: `move_doc.py`
    68	closes a ticket and its RFC together and repairs the citations, `temporary_statements.py` reads
    69	and retires expiring statements, and `docs_corpus.py` is the one view of the tree they share.
    70	They run on the standard library alone. Their behavioral tests are in [`tests/`](../tests/) and
    71	are part of the project's [verification set](../docs/process.md#verification).

input.content:
# Installed harness

**The real skill files live in [`skills/`](./skills/).** Loaders are directory links to that folder:

- Codex — reads `.agents/skills` natively; no link needed.
- Claude Code — `.claude/skills` → `../.agents/skills`
- Cursor — `.cursor/skills` → `../.agents/skills`

The links are tracked as symlinks (mode 120000). Git for Windows writes `core.symlinks=false` on
clone, so they check out as text files. After clone:

```
git config --local core.symlinks true
git checkout -- .claude/skills .cursor/skills
```

Windows needs Developer Mode (Settings → System → For developers) or an elevated prompt to create
a directory symlink. If checkout still yields a file, delete it and run
`mklink /D .claude\skills ..\.agents\skills` (likewise for `.cursor\skills`). Creating these links
is part of the installer's job once it exists; a junction is not an acceptable substitute, git
would track it as a directory.

Which links are actually required is untested. Codex needs none; Cursor documents reading
`.agents/skills` directly; Claude Code may too.

## Mechanical support

[`scripts/`](./scripts/) holds what the harness derives and repairs mechanically: `move_doc.py`
closes a ticket and its RFC together and repairs the citations that pointed at them,
`temporary_statements.py` reads and retires expiring statements, `mechanisms.py` says whether a
mechanism's declaration is true and renders the register from
[`mechanisms/`](./mechanisms/), and `docs_corpus.py` is the one view of the tree they share. They
run on the standard library alone, and their behavioral tests are in [`tests/`](../tests/).

# The remaining named corpus arrives

- **Status:** Partial (four of five installed 2026-09-07; nothing else met)
- **Type:** HITL
- **Depends on:** [Each skill owns its own responsibility](./01-0016-responsibility-coherent.md)
  (so five new skills inherit settled vocabulary and stated ownership rather than adding to the
  restatement)
- **Outcome:** `/advise`, `/skill-up`, `/commit`, `/celebrate` and `/edge` are installed from the
  accepted selection, discoverable, each used once, and the core changes they owe are landed with
  them.

## Parent

[Shared harness across projects](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md), from
[the bootstrap corpus selection](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#bootstrap-corpus-selection).
`/impact`: [the 2026-09-06 split assessment](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#third-bootstrap-delivery--2026-09-06).

## Four arrived early, 2026-09-07

The user installed `/advise`, `/celebrate`, `/commit` and `/skill-up` directly, ahead of this
ticket's align, on the ground that they are useful as they stand. That is a decision, not a
violation — but it lands the files without the adaptations this ticket exists to apply, so what
remains is recorded here rather than assumed done.

**Landed:** the four skill bodies, listed in `AGENTS.md`'s local block and
[`.agents/README.md`](../../.agents/README.md).

**Repaired on landing, under repair-and-report, and then repaired again the same day.**
`/commit`'s `<project-local>` block carried another project's gate set — `ruff check`,
`ruff format --check`, `pyright`, `pytest`, and a `docs/cicd.md` this project does not have.
*"The selection forbids copying another project's test or release commands"* is this ticket's own
rule, below. The first repair substituted this project's commands into the same block, which the
user corrected: **only global practice belongs in a core skill, and a `<project-local>` block should
avoid being an override.** `/commit`'s body already carries the global practice — *run the checks
the repository defines for itself* — so the block was deleted rather than rewritten, and the body
now says explicitly that a commit skill must read a project's commands from where the project states
them and never carry them. How a project's facts arrive at all is a larger question and now has its
own ticket: [01-0010.0110](./01-0010.0110-project-facets-injected.md).

**Still owed, and none of it is done:**

- Each of the four used once on real work here.
- `/commit` reads the autonomy switches from the entry file's local block instead of carrying its
  own absolute *never commit without permission* rule. It still carries the absolute form.
- `/skill-up` documents `<temporary until="...">` alongside `<project-local>`. It documents
  neither.
- ~~**New, found on landing:** `/commit`'s body tags commits `DOCS` / `CODE` / `CICD` / `SKILL`,
  while every commit in this repository is prefixed with the loop's stage. Two vocabularies for one
  field.~~ **Settled 2026-09-07 by the user:** the loop step wins, and it is now defined in
  `/commit`'s body as a global practice — the step that produced the work, uppercase, plus `FIX`
  and `EQUIP` outside the ring (`EQUIP` chosen over `HARNESS` on 2026-09-07: every other prefix is
  a verb, and *to harness* is a verb meaning something else). The prefix says which step produced the work, never which files it
  touched; the diff already shows the second.
- `/skill-up`'s blanket appendix preservation, which the selection says cannot survive.
- `/edge`, which has not arrived, and the `docs/edge/` question below.
- Whether `/celebrate` earns installation at all — now moot as a gate, since it is installed, but
  the selection's reasoning still wants an answer before it is treated as load-bearing.

## Why this exists

Ten of the twenty selected commands remain uninstalled. The user named five of them on 2026-09-06;
`/conclude`, `/recall`, `/dream`, `/review-architecture` and `/setup-devops` stay in the parent's
backlog and are not this ticket's.

Three of the five carry
[core changes owed by later installs](./01-0010-dev-harness-shared-and-local.md#core-changes-owed-by-later-installs),
decided 2026-09-05 and unlanded:

- `/commit`, and any skill gating on permission, reads the autonomy switches from the entry file's
  local block instead of carrying its own absolute rule.
- `/skill-up` documents `<temporary until="...">` alongside `<project-local>`.
- `/edge` reconciles its callers with the actual document inventory — this project has no
  `docs/edge/`, which makes `/maintain`'s Edge-record check currently unguarded prose.

## What to build

This is the decision-bearing phase. Its align decides the split and order; it then decomposes into
children through `/ticket`, one per skill or per mechanism where several belong together — the
precedent being [01-0010.0050](./done/01-0010.0050-install-implement.md), which installed `/implement`,
`/tdd` and `/improve-comments` as one mechanism.

- Selection adaptations named in the corpus table are applied per skill, not assumed.
- `/commit` supplies this project's real checks locally; the selection forbids copying another
  project's test or release commands.
- `/skill-up`'s blanket appendix preservation cannot survive, per the selection; the unresolved
  override policy stays explicit rather than being quietly chosen.
- `/edge` does not create or declare normative Edge records for this project by being installed.

## Decisions this ticket's align owns

- The order and grouping of the five, and whether any belong together as one mechanism.
- Whether `/edge` arriving requires `docs/edge/` to exist, or whether the capability installs
  against an empty inventory with `/maintain`'s check explicitly unguarded until a record exists.
- Whether `/celebrate` earns installation at all — the selection says to retain the capability
  "without making celebration a completion requirement", which is close to saying it changes nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The five are installed under `.agents/skills/`, and a fresh session lists them the way it
  lists `/spec`. **Partial, 2026-09-07:** four landed and are listed; `/edge` has not arrived.
- [ ] Each is used once on real work in this repository.
- [ ] The three owed core changes are landed with their skills, and the parent's owed-changes list
  reflects it.
- [x] ~~`AGENTS.md`'s local block and `.agents/README.md` list them.~~ **Dissolved 2026-09-07**
  during [01-0011.0010](./01-0011.0010-mechanism-declared.md)'s `/plan`, on the user's decision.
  Both rosters were copies — of `.agents/skills/` and of each other — and the host lists the set
  every session. `AGENTS.md`'s `Installed:` line is deleted; `.agents/README.md`'s narrative goes
  with the register. A skill is installed by being in `.agents/skills/`, and nothing restates it.
  The half this loses — *named in the loop but not installed here*, which was `/recall`,
  `/conclude`, `/edge` — is derivable from the entry file's own body against that directory, and
  **nothing derives it today**. Recorded as this ticket's, since `/edge` is one of its five.
- [x] `/commit`'s two vocabularies are reconciled. **2026-09-07:** the loop step wins, defined in
  `/commit`'s body rather than in a local block, because it is a global practice.
- [ ] `/maintain`'s Edge-record check either has records to check or says it has none.
- [ ] `/verify` has been run on this ticket against its ticket, RFC, and governing docs.

## Out of scope

`/conclude`, `/recall`, `/dream`, `/review-architecture`, `/setup-devops` — still the parent's.
The four rule refactors. Cross-project distribution.

## Parent scope addressed

Five of the ten remaining selected commands; three of the six owed core changes.
